NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using RMS vibration amplitude as the leading indicator.  
Novelty departure: A time-domain envelope of high-frequency impact energy, derived from the 1 kHz vibration stream, as a precursor to RMS degradation.  
Physics connection: Inner-race spalling generates periodic high-frequency impacts (ball passing over defect) that increase in amplitude and regularity as the defect grows, detectable before RMS rise due to nonlinear energy accumulation.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Impact energy ∝ (defect depth)² × (contact stiffness) × (passing frequency).  
Direction-of-effect: Driving variable = defect depth; the mechanism detects early increases in impact energy, which rises as spalling progresses, providing warning before RMS threshold.  
Magnitude verification: Impact envelope amplitude scales with (defect depth)²; a 0.2 mm defect (typical spalling initiation) generates 10× higher envelope energy than noise floor (CALCULATED from bearing geometry and Hertzian contact stress).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
MECHANISM CLASS: High-frequency envelope extraction algorithm  
(a) Real-time processing module (software update to existing vibration analyzer) – ALREADY-RECORDED: 1 kHz vibration sensor stream  
(b) Peak detection and envelope extraction algorithm – DERIVED: Stated physics (impact energy ∝ defect depth²)  
(c) Time-series comparator (14-day moving average) – DERIVED: Stated constraint (14-day warning)  
(d) Threshold calculator – DERIVED: Stated spec (2 false alarms/year → 99.99% specificity; CALCULATED from historical noise floor data)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as RMS monitoring (software-only update to existing hardware)  
- Operability: No new training required (uses existing SCADA interface)  
- Maintenance: Zero additional maintenance (algorithm runs on existing infrastructure)  
- Cost class: Software license only ($1k–$5k) vs. RMS hardware ($10k+)  
- Operational loss: Zero throughput/energy penalty (passive monitoring)  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Log envelope amplitude and RMS from 1 kHz vibration stream for 30 days; introduce spall defect via EDM machining at day 10.  
Instruments: Existing 1 kHz sensor, SCADA logging, oscilloscope for validation.  
Pass/fail: Envelope threshold tripped within 14 days of defect initiation; RMS threshold not tripped until day 24.  
Kill criterion: Envelope threshold fails to trip within 14 days of defect initiation.  
Duration: 30 days.  
Validation: Against stated physical relation (impact energy ∝ defect depth²) using pre-recorded baseline noise data.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Envelope amplitude (directly tied to spalling physics per governing relation).  
Secondary indicator: RMS (supplements to reduce false alarms but does not replace envelope).

BILL_UNTAGGED: - Installability: Same as RMS monitoring (software-only update to existing hardware)
- Operability: No new training required (uses existing SCADA interface)
- Maintenance: Zero additional maintenance (algorithm runs on existing infrastructure)
- Cost class: Software license only ($1k–$5k) vs. RMS hardware ($10k+)
- Operational loss: Zero throughput/energy penalty (passive monitoring)
